text:
Montreal arrives at St. Louis on a 3-1-1 run, fresh off a 2-1 win in Winnipeg on Sunday, without Nick Suzuki and Ivan Demidov. Oliver Kapanen has stepped in beside Juraj Slafkovský and Cole Caufield, and Josh Anderson, who plays his 700th NHL game tonight, has taken Demidov's spot beside Slafkovský and Alex Newhook. The Blues are 2-3-0 in their last five and were blanked 4-0 by Carolina on Saturday, without Ross Johnston and Dillon Dube.

The teams are close in the numbers. At five on five, Montreal has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, St. Louis 49%. Our model has it nearly even tonight, 3.18 to 3.05 in Montreal's favor. The Canadiens' weak spot is discipline: 5.4 penalties a game. The Blues kill penalties well, allowing 0.48 expected goals a game on the penalty kill against 0.84 for Montreal.

The goalies split sharply. Montreal's projected starter, Jacob Fowler, has saved 6.0 goals more than the shots deserved this season and is .937 over his last five starts. St. Louis projects Jordan Binnington, at minus 5.6 this season and minus 22.9 last year, in place of Joel Hofer.

Caufield, the top power-play shooter, has a 38% chance to score. For the Blues, Dylan Holloway (26% to score, 60% to get a point) scored twice Thursday, as RotoWire noted.
